It's January 2026. The US just announced a major new AI regulation bill that requires all companies deploying models over 10B parameters to submit safety reports every 6 months and implement mandatory watermarking for generated images and text.

What do you think the biggest practical impact will be on open-source AI developers and hobbyists in the next 1–2 years? Give a short, reasoned opinion (3–5 sentences).

The primary impact will likely be the rapid fragmentation of the open-source ecosystem, as hobbyists and small labs will abandon the 10B parameter threshold to avoid regulatory burdens, pushing the "frontier" of accessible open-source down to smaller, less capable models. This will stifle innovation in the mid-tier model space, forcing developers to either absorb the high compliance costs of watermarking and safety audits or retreat to closed-source platforms that can more easily manage these requirements. Consequently, the open-source community may become less competitive in high-performance tasks, potentially ceding ground to well-funded corporate entities that can navigate the new regulatory landscape.
